newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: BOE jumps on Boland stake talk.
newsitem.headline: BOE jumps on Boland stake talk.

text.p: Shares in The Board of Executors Ltd (BOE) climbed to a fresh high on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Friday as speculation about a sale of a stake in the South African financial services group took a fresh turn.

Dealers and analysts said rumours were circulating that Boland Bank Holdings Ltd, which merged operations with NBS Holdings Ltd in December, may be eyeing a stake in BOE following cautionary notices from both BOE and NBS this week.
"NBS has a cautionary in the paper today and it has made people think that they might be interested in BOE which had a cautionary earlier this week," a JSE dealer said.

This follows talk earlier this week, dismissed as "pure rumour" by Britain's National Westminster Bank Plc (Natwest) that it was set to take a stake in BOE. BOE and Natwest jointly own a merchant banking and stockbroking frim.

Analysts said on Friday BOE and Boland had "historically had close ties and a very good relationship". Phil Biden, the managing director of BOE, sits on the board of Boland and Christo Wiese, Boland's chairman, is on the BOE board.

Analysts said the purchase of a chunk of BOE by acquisitive Boland, which in December bought a 25.6 percent stake in NBS for 1.5 billion rand to form the country's fifth largest banking group, would be a coup for the Western Cape-based firm.
"It will be a great deal for Boland. They will obviously take the crown jewels of BOE -- the asset management company," said Theunis de Bruin, an analyst at Huysamer Stals.
At the time of the acquisition of NBS, Boland said it planned to become a more significant player in the financial services market by forming alliances.
De Bruin was, however, not convinced that a Boland-BOE deal would take place, saying: "But the big question is why would BOE want to sell?".
One benefit to BOE would be to give it access to a large retail network through the enlarged Boland NBS group, he said.
Analysts said any BOE deal would also bring Fidelity Bank, in which BOE holds a 26 percent stake, into the equation.

On Friday morning BOE shares jumped 200 cents to 96 rand, a record high, but by 1130 GMT they had slid back to their overnight closing level of 94 rand. Boland stocks were up 50 cents to 44.50 after 16,700 shares had traded.
